#14232 1 2007-02-26T00:14:06Z usaswim
How to make a KRA

Try to make the race not overlap too much, otherwise there will be a huge empty spot without a tileset, such as in The Tax Man Naked. The reason this map was top rated is because it was the first good KRA and also the flow is stupendous. It could have been better there were more tiles, but that made the race quite longer

Step 1

I recommend you start from the bottom, but you can start anywhere on the map.

Ok, you start from scratch. Before you do anything, place N and the rocket on the page, preferably close together*. First, just make a *flowy* tileset. Don't worry about looks right now. Worry about flow. Jumps are very important. Try to make N go everywhere, and make a long tileset if possible.

*For an excellent KRA, place the N and rocket far apart, but much skill is needed to make a great race

TIP:Try to make the tileset not overlap too much, otherwise, there may be a huge empty spot in the middle.



Step 2

This is when we get serious. Make it so that the rocket will stay alive during the entire thing. Try to make the rocket hug the curves of the tileset. The tileset should be forming.

TIP: Make a demo of your completion. If you aren't a good N-player, ask somebody to demo it for you. Keep that demo everytime you play.



Step 3

By this time, you should be making narrow tunnels for the rocket to travel through. Don't make huge gaps for the rocket to go through. The tunnel where N plays should be wide, but not too wide. Don't make it so that N will have to squeeze through a tube. That is a n00b race. Don't do that. The tileset should be done. Make the tileset look neat and beautiful. Looks like it would make a great playable tileset, eh?



Step 4

This step is the most fun. In this step, you get to add mines, gold, enemies, ect. Please no lag. Nobody ever likes lag. Don't overload it with mines or gold. Stick with the same gold pattern throughout. Don't put random gold everywhere. Or too much of it. Don't put too much of mines either. You should do the enemies last. In this, I added drones for a few lose calls, but not too many, because that would create lag. Use the same demo to playtest your enemies/mines/gold. Make the gold easy to get along the way.
Here is the final result

#304957 4 2007-03-13T17:25:54Z usaswim
I was just like you when I was new to NUMA.

For acronyms, you can go here. Some examples are AGCD (all-gold completion demo), DDA (Don't do anything).

Here, you can find a great resource for good map-making skills.

To improve your grammar, go here.

Here is what makes a map what:

IMPORTANT:

Unfortunately, most new people here don't realize that you should never clump ANYTHING. That includes enemies and objects. Make the tileset look as good as possible. Also, do not hide trap doors that trap N in, so it cannot excape. Those are terribly unfun maps.
  • Survival - It should usually not include exits.
  • Race - Should be very flowy and should only have one path to follow.
  • Action - You must find the best path. There are many maps that fall under this category.
  • Incomplete - Of course, this is for incomplete maps only.
  • Test Level - This is for testing new concepts.
  • Tileset - non-playable. To make a picture using tiles.
  • N-Art - most are non-playable. For designs.This is an example of N-Art you must play.
  • DDA - Don't do anything or hold one button. There are many types, from a KRA (Keep rocket alive) to a HRDEKRADDA (Hold Right, Door Eerie, Keep the Rocket Alive, Don't do Anything). There is also a newer concept, which is Chase the rocket.
  • Puzzle - This is for complicated puzzles. Not as in a jigsaw puzzle.
  • Uncategorized - Category doesn't exist anymore.

#305252 7 2007-03-14T22:03:37Z usaswim
What maps are hardest to make?

Well, generally, a DDA is usually the hardest to make. It involves lots of testing and will also take the longest time. I highly recommend using a wide variety of propulsion. Here is a great place to learn about DDAs.

Test levels may take a bit of thinking to make too. N-Arts generally take up the most time. They require lots of experience and effort.

Which maps are easiest to make?

That depends on how much time you spend and how good you want the map to be. Survivals, tilesets, and action are usually the easiest.

Which maps are the most fun to make?

That depends on the mood you're in. I like to make races and DDAs. N-Arts are partially fun to make as well as tilesets. They may become quite frustrating, though. Action can be quite fun too.

Which maps are the most boring to make?

I'd have to go with survivals. They take up the least amount of time, and it is quite hard to come up with a good one. Puzzles can be a bit tricky and may not be as fun as you might expect.

Which maps are the longest to make?

N-Arts. They can take months. DDAs aren't far behind.

Which maps are shortest to make?

Preferably action or survival. Survival takes the least amount of time, and actions can vary from minutes to days.

#305683 8 2007-03-16T21:28:42Z usaswim
Yes, I hated that level to death but it wasn't my least favorite. It wasn't hard after I did it a few times. So, you can get up. Good. Now all you need to do is go down. You wait until all the drones are at the bottom, and then climb onto the right wall. Make the drone chase you. After a while hanging there, jump to the left wall and make the drone notice you. You should be about 1/2 down by now. There is probably one drone left. Keep next the the wall (don't hang onto it!) that drone is on, and jump off when you are close to the drone. By now, the other two drones have probably turned back, so you go must go to the bottom. Grab hold of the wall at the very bottom right so you won't die. On the other side, collect ALL of the gold. If you go halfway, the gauss will kill you as you leap off. The rocket isn't too hard to dodge.

#305700 12 2007-03-16T21:54:45Z usaswim
Well, there is an easier approach to the "hounds" level. Stand right next to switch, and you will be barely touching it. If you do it right, the lock won't open due to object overlapping delay.

I can't help much on 29-4 because I skipped it and got the flavor instead.

About 29-3:
Rocket dodging isn't very difficult if you know the right path. The high scores demonstrate that path, although mine is the slower version. After you get out of the pit, jump to the left most wall and when you almost reach the bottom, jump again and go to the gold area and get the gold by wall jumping once. Immediately go for the bottom. Slow down when you reach the thwump, and the rest is pretty easy. Go back up by wall jumping until you get to the very top and then leap onto that slanted platform. Immediately jump sideways at a 45 degree angle to the right. The rockets should crash into the ceiling. On the right side, I just jumped onto the very right platform and then jumped again dodging mines. Land on the slope, and make sure the chaingun doesn't see you. I didn't get the gold.

#14622 1 2007-03-28T17:18:06Z usaswim
Ok, there have been a lot of duplicate topics about topics that have been discussed millions of times before and are in the FAQs, etc. So please don't post additional topics and read this instead!

Brief FAQ

How come I have to click my mouse in order for something to happen?

You have frame-by-frame mode on. Make sure your caps lock is on to play in normal mode

N is running slower than usual. Is there any way I can boost performance?

Yes. There may be background programs running that are using up memory. Close those. You can also change the priority of N. Go to task manager > n_v14.exe > right-click > Set Priority > High (or above-normal). Also check the system requirements to make sure your computer is able to run N v1.4 smoothly.

System Requirements:

1024x768pixel screen resolution
fast processor: Pentium 3 ~800MHz is the general minimum. Pentium 4 equivalent or better is recommended.

AGP video card recommended.

I've made an awesome map and I'm trying to submit it to NUMA. However, I don't have an account, and there is no register link anywhere. How do I register to NUMA?!?

You must have N v1.4.
  1. Open it
  2. Go to configure
  3. You will see three textboxes labeled username, password, and email.
  4. Enter your desired username, password, and (optional) email. *Make your password difficult to guess. Choose a "good" username, one that is not insulting. Do not include spaces, as they will be ommited.
  5. Press create new user.
I have completed the entire column except for the very last level, but I have the flavor! Is this some sort of bug? SWEET!

No, it is not a bug. You get a new flavor after you reach the last level of that column. You will also get the first secret after completing any six columns.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Forum Rules

Shall we? Yes, the good 'ol rule book. Now don't break them!

Forum Rules

How to play other people's maps (or yours)
  1. Go to the map that you want to play on NUMA and copy the 1.4+ Map Data.
  2. If you want to play it using frame-by-frame (FBF), skip to #8
    If you want to play it whenever you feel like it (userlevels), skip to #19
    Alternative- skip to #27
    If you want to play it only once, without FBF, proceed to #3
  3. Open N and press userlevels.
  4. Copy the data onto the textbox on the lower left and press watch replay.
  5. Play the map. If you die, press return to menu (on the bottom left)
  6. If you complete the map, your demo data will be automatically saved onto the textbox.
    This is how you get your demo:
    Here's an excerpt of the data : 0,1,25,9,0,-1,0#1895:71582796|7158278
    Everything that is underlined is the demo data. It is everything past the # sign.
  7. If you want to watch your demo, just press watch replay.
  8. Open N and press ~.
  9. Delete everything from the level data textbox and paste the map data onto the level data textbox.
  10. Click somewhere OUTSIDE of the Level Data Box to avoid getting NaN's.
  11. Press L
  12. Press 1 to record demo
  13. Press P IMPORTANT: Make sure you have caps lock on!
  14. If you die, press ~.
  15. Press R to reset objects.
  16. Repeat steps 11-14 until you complete the map.
  17. If you complete the map, press ~
  18. Your demo will be saved onto the demo data textbox.
  19. Press P to watch your demo. IMPORTANT: Do not press 1 unless you want to play the level over!
  20. Open the folder you downloaded N to. IMPORTANT: If the files are scattered, place them inside the same folder. Make sure that the N v1.4 you start up is in the same folder as the userlevels.txt. Do not delete that N v1.4 if you create a shortcut somewhere.
  21. Open userlevels.txt. Instructions are in the txt if you want to read it. Otherwise, read this.
  22. Paste the 1.4+ Map Data below the line. You can put it anywhere below the line. It doesn't matter. Do not paste the data inside another map data. Paste it on a new line. Make sure it is in this format - ($Level name#Author#Category#Map data#)
  23. Press File > Save
  24. Open N and press userlevels
  25. Wait for parsing data. The load time depends on how big the userlevels.txt file is. Now find the map. Click it.
  26. If you beat the level, your demo will be in the textbox. Go to #6 for information about it.
  27. Your personal best will be displayed on the right of that map. Press it to watch your personal best.
  28. Go here and download the Firefox numADD extension. IMPORTANT: You must be using Firefox.
  29. Go to the link and download it.
  30. Select "Open with Firefox"
  31. Install it and restart Firefox
  32. Right-click the menu bar at the top (The area with File, Edit, View, etc.)
  33. Select Customize
  34. Scroll down, find numADD, and drag it to any location on the browser you want
  35. Press the down arrow, select "change userlevels.txt position"
  36. IMPORTANT: Make sure the extracted files (n_v14.exe, userlevels.txt, editors_manual.txt, etc.) are in one folder
    Locate that folder, find userlevels.txt, and select it.
  37. Do the same with "change N executable position". Find n_v14 and select it.
  38. Go to NUMA, find the map you want to add to userlevels.txt, and press the button.
How to make maps
  1. Open N and go to NED (Press ~)
  2. From here, you have 2 options, you can load a full map or an empty map. A full map is where the entire map is covered with tiles. An empty map is just... empty.
  3. Press E to edit the map
  4. If you want to put objects on the map first, go to #9
    If you want to put tiles on first, proceed to #5
  5. Press delete to go to tile editor.
  6. From here, you have a variety of choices. You can use gridlines first of all. Gridlines are similar to lines on graph paper.
  7. The gridline letters are displayed on the box thing. Press those letters and see which one suits you best. Gridlines aren't necessary. I personally like H the best.
  8. I won't explain how to put tiles on, because it's pretty much self-explanatory. Refer to the editor's manual for instructions.
  9. Press insert to go the object editor.
  10. There are gridlines here, as well. Refer to #6-7 to learn about gridlines.
  11. Cursor snapping is how you want to put the objects on. Z-snap will look extremely ugly if you don't use it correctly. Do not overlap gold or mines (unless you want gold delay). I also recommend you don't overlap rockets, gausses, or launchpads. X-snap is 1/2 snap, and C-snap is 1/4 snap, which is smaller.
  12. To select an object, press the number or letter of the object. Press the letter or letter combinations of the object you want to place. Hold the letter and click to place.
  13. Hold backspace and press an object to delete it. Sometimes it may not be accurate
  14. TIP: Hold \ and press anywhere to delete the most recent object.
  15. Have fun!
  16. Press home to go back to editing menu
  17. Press ~ to go back to debug menu
  18. The level data will be saved on the level data textbox. Copy that and save it somewhere, or send it to NUMA.
How to watch demos

There are 2 ways. In some maps, it won't work in userlevels. It will only work in debug mode. Such things that may not work in userlevels are DDAs, glitches, cheating death.

Userlevels
  1. Open N and press userlevels
  2. Copy the map data first, and paste it onto the textbox.
  3. Copy the demo data and paste it after the map data.
  4. Press watch replay.
Debug mode
  1. Open N and press ~
  2. Copy the map data onto the level data textbox and press L
  3. Copy the demo data onto the demo data textbox and press 3
  4. Press P IMPORTANT: Make sure caps lock is on!
Concerning FBF

Frame-by-frame (FBF) is a method used for maps that require precision or if you just want to go fast.
  1. Open N and press ~
  2. Paste the map data and press L
  3. Press 1 to record demo
  4. Press P IMPORTANT: Make sure caps lock is off!
  5. As you can see, everything is still and there is no movement. Click your mouse for 1 frame to move by.
  6. You can turn on caps lock anytime if you want to play in normal mode and turn off caps lock if you want to play in FBF mode. Such things that FBF may come in handy are
    Spoiler: chimney-jumping
    Spoiler: triple jumps
    Spoiler: triple jump off bounce block
    There are many more possibilities.
  7. FBF takes practice, and is difficult to master in a few tries.
How to save your N progress

So you won't have to start over!

Quote: .sol files for dummies
Introduction

The n_v14b_userdata.sol, or ".sol", is the file that contains all your N peference datas. That includes your Configuration settings, your progress in your game, your personal bests, etc. With this file, you can move around your progress in the game to other computers and such so that you won't need to start all over on a new computer, as that can be quite tiresome.

Location

*note that some files/folders are hidden. To view them, go to Control Panel > (Classic View) > Folder Options > View tab > Show hidden files and folders

Windows Vista

Computer>OS (C:)>Users>username>AppData>Roaming>Macromedia>FlashPlayer>#SharedObjects>Random numbers or letters>localhost

Windows XP

C:>Documents and Settings>Username>Application Data>Macromedia>Flash Player>#SharedObjects>random series of letters and numbers>localhost
  1. Go to the location of the .sol file
  2. IMPORTANT: Do not open/delete the .sol file unless you want to erase all current N progress (including cheated levels)
  3. Copy the file by right-clicking it and pressing copy
  4. Paste it onto a different location on your computer, one that you can locate easily
Concerning Teleporters

It is difficult to explain it here, so you must go to the link to learn.

Teleporter Tutorial

Increasing N experience

Do you ever feel like a n00b? Ever think you will never manage to finish N let alone get high scores? Well, you aren't alone! Go here for you complimentary 4-year scholarship to St. Atilla's College for Ninja!

For everything else, please read the readme.txt and the editors_manual for extra information. (It's there for a reason!) It is really annoying, if you didn't realize, to have so many multiple topics about the same thing.

I have a LOT of thoughts.

1 - Waking Up - Way too simple, back & forth is always boring, not a single enemy, just bland. 1/5

2 - Fault Line - That is a LOT of drones. I have no idea how to get that switch. The closest I've ever gotten to it was 5 pixels away. Too difficult for most. 2/5

3 - The Recipe - WTF. WAYYYY too many enemies, I die instantly when I attempt to get the first switch because either machine gun drone kills me or the seeker drone kills me first. Extremely difficult and not very entertaining. 1/5

4 - Cast it Out - Very good. The bottom part with all those mines is just infuriating. I cannot get past that floorguard despite all my attempts. The room right above it with the 3 rockets is also pretty difficult. The floorguard just makes everything hard because you are forced to jump and hit the rocket. I can't seem to get that switch on the top right no matter what. 3.5/5

5 - Wasteland - Not too easy nor too difficult. Fun. Much simpler. 4/5

6 - Seasons to Cycle - The rocket part was very entertaining but the mines weren't as fun. The thwump part really got on my nerves. The laser part was a lot more difficult than I expected. 4/5

7 - Half Life - The bottom part REALLY got me frustrated. The rest is ok. 3/5

8 - Through the Iris - The top part is really fun, but the bottom part is a lot less fun due to the difficulty. The gauss is just annoying as hell. The top part is great to practice corner jumping, and I made a pretty nice jump that I am damn proud of although highscorers do it all the time. 4/5

#314333 12 2007-04-19T21:13:07Z usaswim
  1. Make it look very attractive
  2. Make it not too easy, nor too hard
  3. Add gold, unless the theme is no gold, in clumps
  4. Tileset is crucial. If you spent under 5 minutes on the tileset it will probably not look nice
  5. Always playtest
  6. Make sure you reset your objects
DDAs
  1. Press 1 before you playtest it
  2. Add enemies first
  3. Don't use random z-snap clumping
  4. Don't overuse gold or mines
  5. Don't make lines and lines of launchpads
  6. Use a variety of propulsion
  7. Make lots of close calls
Races
  1. Make it very flowy
  2. Don't overuse launchpads (exception of no-jump races)
  3. Add an adequate amount of gold and mines (if necessary)
  4. Don't make too many close calls
  5. Don't overuse enemies (especially machine-gun drones)
  6. Don't make tunnel races (where the floor-ceiling is 1 unit) involving lots of 4 and 8 tiles.
For everything else... check here

#317300 2 2007-05-01T04:37:17Z usaswim
I'm 100% positive this is in the forums somewhere because I personally did this once to somebody.

Action
These maps come in a variety of different shapes, sizes, smells, etc. It is the simplest group with the simplest rules.

Requirements:
  • If your map doesn't fit into any of the categories below, it may be considered action
DDA
A DDA stands for "Don't do anything". Yes, in these maps, they were designed to let you sit back and enjoy the show. Kinda like watching a movie. A DDA guide provided by Clifty (the king of DDAs), gets more in-depth about the sub-categories of DDAs. Most DDAs usually require you to press "1" before playing. A good DDA includes the following:
  • Lots of close calls
  • A good number of enemies
  • All enemies are involved
  • N is not wandering away from enemies frequently
  • Teleporters are quite bad in DDAs unless crucial
  • A variety of propulsion
  • Minimal lag
  • No long waiting periods with no enemy actions
The list could go on forever.

Requirements:
  • Don't do anything, or hold left or hold right.
Incomplete
This is the category for, you guessed it! Incomplete maps. If you don't have time to finish a map, is too lazy, ashamed of it, giving others a sneak preview, or saving it for later, you can submit your map under Incomplete. Of course, there is NUPB (The N User's Paste Bin). It is a place where you can save your map data so you can continue working on it later. It can serve for many different purposes, not just that one. There is also Mapswap. If you just cannot finish a map, you can trade your unfinished map for somebody else's unfinished map. You can finish their map and submit it to NUMA. But be sure to credit them!

Requirements
  • Unfinished maps only
N Art
This is the category for masterpieces created using tiles or objects. Some people have experimented with blending colors (placing objects within close proximity so when viewed in a thumbnail, the colors appear blended) to make green, purple, orange, etc, etc. A good N-Art is neat, colorful, and looks good (duh). Some N-Arts you must load in order to see the effects. Some include N-Snake.

Requirements:
  • Should not be usable to create a map
Puzzle
This category contains puzzle maps. No, not a jigsaw puzzle. These are maps that force you to use your brain cells.

Requirements
  • They should be able to make you think
Race
These maps are the most fun (IMO) to play. They are usually destined to have 1 specific route you must follow. Some races are multi-route however. These races should have very good flow and lots of jumps. Enemies should be used throughout the race and spread evenly. Races with gausses in every corner aren't good races. Also, it doesn't look good. Good looking tilesets will attract the audience's attention to play it.

Requirements:
  • Must have a specific route
  • Flow is crucial
Survival
These maps have no exits. It is an endurance test to see how long N can survive while dodging many enemies. Overly difficult survivals aren't very fun.

Requirements:
  • No exit
  • Should have a good amount of enemies to keep N busy
  • No dead spots (places in which you can last forever or a very long time)
Test Level
This category is mainly for new concepts. They are never before seen concepts that have never been used in maps.

Requirements:
  • Must be a new(ish) concept
  • Can be playable or not playable
Tileset
Tilesets are tiles arranged to make different shapes and designs. It is partially like N-Art except the tilesets can be used to make maps. The better looking, the higher the rating. Of course, it also depends on the usability.

Requirements:
  • Should have empty space to use for a map
  • Good looking
Uncategorized
This category is no longer used. This category is used for maps that just cannot fit any of the above categories.

Actually kkstrong0, the definition of a "head rhyme" is a rhyming sequence with constant alliteration. Alliteration needs more than one word, like "Jack picked a peck of pickled peppers". Many of those words have the "p" sound in them, so therefore, it qualifies as alliteration.

So basically, a head rhyme is another word for alliteration.

Ahh... I just finished Maximum Ride. It is totally the pwnzorz book to read. It's a book that you would love. Some people may not like it. If you don't like spine-tingling suspense, with LOTS of action, this isn't the book for you. There is so much suspense. I just had to keep on reading until I got to the end. I totally this book. Totally pwns Harry Potter. I stayed up until 1 or 2 last night, I just couldn't put the book down. I forced myself to stop reading. Well, I kinda fell asleep.
Spoiler: [bExcerpt[/b]]
Okay. I'm Max. I'm fourteen. I live with my family, who are five kids not related to me by blood, but still totally my family.
We're-well, we're kind of amazing. Not to sound too full of myself, but we're like nothing you've ever seen before.
Basically, we're pretty cool, nice, smart - but not "average" in any way. The six of us - me, Fang, Iggy, Nudge, the Gasman, and Angel - were made on purpose, by the sickest, most horrible "scientists" you could possibly imagine. They created us as an experiment. An experiment where we ended up only 98 percent human. That other 2 percent has had a big impact, let me tell you. We grew up in a science lab/prison called the School, in cages, like lab rats. It's pretty amazing we can think or speak at all. But we can - and so much more.
There was one other School experiment that made it past infancy. Part human, part wolf - all predator: They're called Erasers. They're tough, smart, and hard to control. They look human, but when they want to, they are capable of morphing into wolf men, complete with fur, fangs, and claws. The School uses them as guards, police - and executioners.
To them, we're six moving targets - prey smart enough to be a challenge. Basically, they want to rip out throats out. And make sure the world never finds out about us.
But I'm not lying down just yet. I'm telling you, right?
This story could be about you - or your children. If not today, then soon. So please, please take this seriously. I'm risking everything that matters by telling you - but you need to know.

Welcome to our nightmare.

Here's another amazing book.

The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time

Don't you just hate books that have the most boring beginnings? They are so tiring to read. We are always looking for a book with an amazing beginning, one that will make you want to read it. This book has just that.

It's about a boy (Christopher) who is quite smart. One night, he goes to his neighbor's yard and finds a dead poodle with a garden fork sticking in it. Christopher loved that dog. He stroked the poodle and wondered who killed him, and why. He pulls the garden fork out of the poodle (who's name is Wellington btw), and hugs it. Christopher loves dogs. He hugged it for 4 minutes until he heard screaming. Mrs. Shears, his neighbor and owner of the poodle, came out and cried, "What in fucks name have you done to my dog?"

As you can see, Christopher is in a very tight situation and it's only the beginning of the book. A must read.

#325525 17 2007-05-29T23:38:05Z usaswim
1. Never carry too much for too long unless it is necessary.
2. Walk with a sense of purpose. If you are wandering aimlessly or look lost you become a target.
3. Act and dress like a local. Tourists are frequent targets of muggers.
4. Carry a weapon where it is permitted. Pepper spray, a 4 inch lockback pocketknife, or a pistol (9mm or 38 caliber minimum for stopping power) will give you confidence that muggers will sense and steer away from. This of course assumes you know how to use your weapon and are carrying it in such a manner that it is unlikely it can be used against you.
5. Learn a martial art, at least the basics. In cases where weapons are not an option, you need to know you can defend yourself with your hands and feet (and head) if necessary. Your confidence radiates outwards and protects you from feral humans who can sense fear.
6. When you sense danger, don't be afraid to act a little crazy. Walking down the middle of the street, and/or singing a song at the top of your lungs will make you a less attractive target. This contradicts the above advice of "not drawing attention to yourself", but when it seems that the attention is already there, it's time to act to discourage action.
7. Determine the risk factor of you getting mugged or robbed. These are the things that let you outweigh your risk of being robbed.
*
o Clothes: Are you dressed like a rich person? Do you have fancy jewelery? Are you wearing a T-shirt and jeans or a suit?
o What you're carrying: Are your hands empty or are you carrying a briefcase, backpack, or suitcase?
o The area you are in: Is it an urban area with a lot of foot traffic, or a suburban neighborhood with few pedestrians?
o How long you will be traveling: The longer you are on the streets, the higher the odds of you passing by at least one thief.

#326389 5 2007-06-01T23:48:09Z usaswim
And you had a week to back-up your .sol file
  1. Did you open your .sol file? If no, skip to #2
  2. Did you misplace your .sol file? If no, skip to #3
  3. Did you rename your .sol file? If no, skip to #4
  4. Did you delete your .sol file? If no, skip to #5
  5. Did you play with the settings and change how much space N can use on your computer? If no, then skip to #6
  6. Did you eat your .sol file? If no, skip to #7
  7. I'm sorry, in this case it's a mystery how you lost your level data
1 - Never open your .sol file without the right software. It will change the extension.
2 - If you misplaced it, replace it back to the right place. The location of your .sol file can be found in this thread.
3 - If you renamed it, DON'T. Change it back to the default name (n_v14b_userdata)
4 - If you deleted you .sol file, it should be in the Recycle Bin. A new .sol file should have taken its place. First restore the deleted .sol file, and get rid of the .sol file that was automatically created. Be sure it's the right name, otherwise it will just create another empty .sol file.
5 - NEVER PLAY WITH THE LOCAL STORAGE. The bar should be slid all the way to the right (Unlimited)
6 - Please don't eat your .sol file.

Players

Map-Makers
Round 5 - This week's theme is symmetry! I will be lenient on the symmetry. You can make everything perfectly symmetrical or you can loosely make it symmetrical. The objects don't have to be perfectly symmetrical, basically the overall look of symmetry in the map.

-------
Spoiler: [imghttp://i193.photobucket.com/albums/z2/usaswim/Action-Packed%20Comp/rulescopy-1.png[/img]]
What about it?
The Action-Packed Competition/Tournament is where users compete making maps and highscoring. The map that scores highest will be placed in front of the players. The user that achieves the highest time will win, as well as the user that made the map that scored the highest based on the criteria. Unlike a tournament, however, players will not be eliminated every round, because this isn't a ladder tournament. The player and map-maker with the most points by the end of the competition wins. This is a 10-week competition. Every week is a new round. While map-makers are making their maps for the next round, players will be submitting their demos from the previous round, so we can save time. For example, while map-makers are making their maps for Round 2, players are submitting their demos for the winning map on Round 1. You may enter in both positions (map-maker and player).

The Rules
Map-Makers
  • All maps must be action.
  • Maps cannot be maps already submitted to NUMA. They must be new maps made after a round has started.
  • All maps must have an exit.
  • Collabs are not allowed.
  • Maps must be appropriate for high-scoring (meaning that there may NOT be any race elements in the map)
  • Maps will be judged based on the categories.
  • Mapmakers can join at any point of the competition. The mapmaker with the most points by the end of the competition will be considered the winner.
  • Map-makers have 1 week to submit their entries.
  • The highest and lowest judge scores for each map will be excluded (similar to the Olympics).
  • Judges may enter.
  • Map-makers may make as many as 2 maps.
  • If 2 or more maps get the same score, the winning map will be decided based on a poll.
Players
  • Players may join even after the competition has begun. The player with the most points by the end of the competition is considered the winner.
  • Absolutely NO FBF.
  • AGD's are not required.
  • Demos will be judged just like the highscoring system; the player with the most time wins.
  • Players have 1 week to submit their demoes.
  • Judges may enter.
  • You may only submit 1 demo per map per week
  • PM me the demoes
  • If 2 or more people get the same time, then the map that scored second will be the map that those people will compete on. This pattern continues.
The Scoring System
Map-Makers and Players
1st - 5 points
2nd - 4 points
3rd - 3 points
4th - 2 points
5th - 1 point
Everyone else - 0

The Judging System
For map-makers only

All maps are judged based on this criteria:

Tileset x/5 (For Round 4 only)
Originality x/5
Aesthetics x/10
Gameplay x/15

x/30

Prizes

1st - Uber sigtag and awesome dedication
2nd - Uber sigtag
3rd - Amazing sigtag

window.Blink = function(args){
// Set the color and seconds below, e.g., [args,'COLOR',SECONDS]
args = (/,/.test(args))? args.split(/,/): [args,'#FFD100',10];
var who = document.getElementById(args[0]);
var count = parseInt(args[2]);
if (--count <=0) {
who.style.backgroundColor = '';
if(who.focus) who.focus();
} else {
args[2]=count+'';
who.style.backgroundColor=(count%2==0)? '': args[1];
args='\"'+args.join(',')+'\"';
setTimeout("Blink("+args+")",500);
}
}


function addLoadEvent(func) {
var oldonload = window.onload;
if (typeof window.onload != 'function') {
window.onload = func;
} else {
window.onload = function() {
if (oldonload) {
oldonload();
}
func();
}
}
}

});

Pie
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Jump to: navigation, search
This article or section is missing citations and/or footnotes.

This article or section contains insufficiently sourced phrases. Using inline citations helps guard against copyright violations and factual inaccuracies. You may improve the article or discuss this issue on its talk page. Help on using footnotes is available. This article has been tagged since May 2007.

This article is about the baked good. For the mathematical constant, see Pi. For other uses, see Pie (disambiguation).

A slice cut from an apple pie
A slice cut from an apple pie

A pie is a baked food, with a baked shell usually made of pastry that covers or completely contains a filling of fruit, meat, fish, vegetables, cheeses, creams, chocolate, custards, nuts, or other sweet or savoury ingredients. Pies can be either "one-crust," where the filling is placed in a dish and covered with a pastry/potato mash top before baking, or "two-crust," with the filling completely enclosed in the pastry shell. Some pies have only a bottom crust, generally if they have a sweet filling that does not require cooking. These bottom-crust-only pies may be known as tarts or tartlets. An example of a bottom-crust-only pie that is savoury rather than sweet is a quiche. Tarte Tatin is a one-crust fruit pie that is served upside-down, with the crust underneath. Blind-baking is used to develop a crust's crispiness, and keep it from becoming soggy under the burden of a very liquid filling. If the crust of the pie requires much more cooking than the chosen filling, it may also be blind-baked before the filling is added and then only briefly cooked or refrigerated. Pie fillings range in size from tiny bite-size party pies or small tartlets, to single-serve pies (e.g. a pasty) and larger pies baked in a dish and eaten by the slice. The type of pastry used depends on the filling. It may be either a butter-rich flaky or puff pastry, a sturdy shortcrust pastry, or, in the case of savoury pies, a hot water crust pastry.

Occasionally the term pie is used to refer to otherwise unrelated confections containing a sweet or savoury filling, such as Eskimo pie or moon pie.

Regional variations

Pies with fillings such as pork, steak and kidney, minced beef or chicken and mushroom are popular in the United Kingdom as take-away snacks. They are also served with chips as an alternative to fish and chips at British chip shops. The residents of Wigan are so renowned for their preference for this food-stuff that they are often referred to as "Pie Eaters" (though the historical reasons for this title are disputed). In honour of this, the main ingredient of a 'Wigan kebab' is the pie, which is placed in a barm cake to make up the popular local delicacy. The combination of pie and mash is traditionally associated with London. Shepherd's pie (which does not involve pastry) is also a favourite amongst people throughout Britain.

Fruit pies may be served with a scoop of ice cream, a style known in North America as la mode. Apple pie is a traditional choice, though any pie with sweet fillings may be served la mode. This pie is thought to have been popularized in the mid-1890s in the United States.

The Australian meat pie has an iconic cultural status, being held to be the Australian National Food[citation needed]. These meat pies contain beef and gravy in a shortcrust piecase, often with a flakey top. The many different types of small commercially-produced pies are popular forms of takeaway food in Australia and New Zealand, with one of the most widespread brands in Australia being Four'N Twenty Pie. Many bakeries and specialty stores sell gourmet pies for the more discriminating customer. A peculiarity of Adelaide cuisine is the Pie floater.

History

The pie has been around since about 2000 B.C., around the time of the ancient Egyptians. At some point between 1400 B.C. (the time of Greek settlements) and 600 B.C. (the time of the decline of Egypt), the pie is believed to have been passed on to the Greeks by the Egyptians.

From Greece the pie spread to Rome, somewhere around 100 B.C. by which time pies had already been around for some 1000 years. The first known pie recipe came from the Romans and was for a rye-crusted goat cheese and honey pie.

Pies appeared in England in the 12th century and were predominantly meat pies. The crust of the pie was referred to as the coffyn and there was generally more crust than filling. Sometimes these pies were made with fowl and the legs were left outside the pie to act as handles. For a long time the pastry crust was actually not eaten, serving only to preserve the moisture and flavour of the filling.

Pies went to America with the first English settlers. As in Roman times the early American pie crusts were not eaten, but simply designed to hold the filling. Today, virtually every country in the world has some form of pie.

Pie throwing

Cream filled or topped pies are favourite props for humour, particularly when aimed at the pompous. Throwing a pie in a person's face has been a staple of film comedy since the early days of the medium, and is often associated with clowns in popular culture. Pranksters have taken to targeting politicians and celebrities with their pies, an act called pieing. Activists sometimes engage in the pieing of political and social targets as well. One such group is the Biotic Baking Brigade. "Pieing" can result in injury to the target and assault or more serious charges against the pie throwers [1]. In Des Moines, Iowa, in 1977, singer and anti-gay-rights activist Anita Bryant became one of the first persons to be "pied" as a political act.[citation needed] See List of people who have been pied.

#330242 2 2007-06-12T01:10:03Z usaswim
The taskbar, on the bottom on the screen? You can't install or uninstall that And you most certainly can't end the process, because there is none!

Just move your mouse over it, and when it pops up, right-click an empty stop in it. Go to Properties. On the Taskbar tab, uncheck "Auto-hide the taskbar". Press Apply, then OK.

That should be the solution. If not, there may be other softwares affecting it. ObjectDock is one program that can control the visibility of the taskbar. If you've uninstalled it previously, re-install it. Once it's there, press the icon that says "Configure Dock". On the General tab, make sure "Hide the Windows Taskbar" is unchecked. Then uninstall it, or keep it (I recommend keeping it )

Here are my opinions about that map:

1) Tileset. Too simple, too basic, but not aesthetically pleasing. Seems random with no theme. Unbeneficial.

2) Object placement. I recommend not attaching gold onto tiles. Don't line them up side by side like that. It's not aesthetically pleasing. Mine placement seems out of place, awkward, and ugly.

3) Locked doors. You overused them. Going back and forth everywhere to collect those isn't fun. At all. Moreover, surrounding objects and enemies with locked doors is horrendously ugly and just destroys looks. It's terribly ugly when you do that and it's inconvenient. I recommend changing the tileset so you only have to place a locked door on 1 side. It looks so much better that way.

4) Enemy placement. Place enemies where you can take full advantage of it. Don't overuse enemies just so you can cover up the entire map. "Recycle" enemies. Put them in frequently visited places. Don't stack enemies next to each other unless it's aesthetically pleasing.

5) One ways. Don't just put them wherever you want. Put them in places where they might come in handy. Placing them is large quantities side by side looks ugly, in my opinion, and is definitely not aesthetically pleasing.

--Made with VB .net--

Just a small application I made. My dad was a really good help.

So basically, enter in the map's information, and demo (optional), and out comes it in userlevels format! You can save it as a text file onto your computer as well. Sooo... that's it? I doubt it was really necessary, but I'm bored everyday anyway.

Something new on v1.0 is the multi map integration. It allows you to upload .txt files of maps you have already made and convert them into a userlevels format. You can upload as many maps as you want. All you do is enter the author name and pack name, and look for the .txt files. The file name will be the map name.

The new feature in v2.0 is that you have the ability to read your userlevels.txt file and browse through all of your maps! It doesn't matter if you have 10, or 10,000 maps in there! It will upload them in mind-blowing speeds! I uploaded the entire Vehemence x 2 (2200 maps!) in the blink of an eye. No, literally. It loads millions of times faster than N. And when you click the map, the data appears in the textbox.

#330921 25 2007-06-13T18:56:11Z usaswim
I could give you advice on races and DDAs.

DDAs
  • No clustering ANYTHING. EVER.
  • Rarely, if ever, use launchpads
  • Make it a good length
  • Don't EVER use gausses unless you use lots of them. They are seemingly pointless, and makes the map more difficult to make than it should. (Though I plan to make a gauss-only DDA sometime...)
  • Use an enemy as efficiently as possible. Don't just use it once, and then throw it away (as in, use a trap door to block a rocket)
  • If there's lots of rockets, don't just make them all die at once, because it's so unprofessional. Just find a way to escape them.
  • No teleporters. If you teleport all the way across the map, it's going to be really hard to follow, and is just an excuse to escape an enemy
  • Try to at least make the tileset somewhat attracting
  • Use a variety of propulsion
  • Use as much space in the map as possible. Empty spaces are just... no.
  • Making close calls is the most important thing. As long as there are uber close calls, everything else won't matter
  • It has got to be fun to watch
  • Don't make it take years to load. Short loading times often tend to make people watch it again.
  • Never use gold delay
  • No lag. Lagging just confuses people
Races
  • Tileset. Make it sexy.
  • Flow is very important
  • The entire map has to have a central theme. Nothing can be random, unless random is the theme of the map, but it has to be pretty obvious
  • Gold placement and amount is important
  • A few mines wouldn't hurt
  • Occupy lots of space
  • Don't make it follow a same path more than twice. It's just an excuse to make it longer.

#15688 1 2007-06-14T03:27:29Z usaswim
Here's a collection of all known glitches/bugs.
Have spoilers turned ON

Common bugs; fixable
Special bugs; no solution thus far
Undefined

Glitches/Bugs in NED
Spoiler: [color=GREENNaN (Not a Number)]When an object is around the edge of the map, it's usually because there's an NaN in the code. Drones can be frozen by placing NaN at the end of the code. NaNs can create remarkable glitches in N. The possibilities are endless.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDTriple-jump/Enemy glitch]Demo data malfunctions during a triple-jump when enemies are removed from the map data[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENGlitched tiles]I don't have much knowledge in this category, but it's basically a tile that looks solid, but you can actually walk through it. Other glitched tiles will act as propulsion, flinging you back when you try to approach it. Some can kill you[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDFloorgaurds not placed on land can crash N]If multiple (or in some cases, just one) floorgaurd/s are not placed on a tile, there is a possibility it will crash Flash Player if you attempt to load level data. I believe it creates an infinite loop. Here is an example[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENOne-ways]One-ways are the most commonly glitched objects. Here is a topic naming all known glitches used with one-ways[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENSome floorgaurds will travel on doors; others won't]lord_day - If you place the door before you place the floorguard, then the floorguard will travel on it. If you place the door after you place the floorguard, then the floorguard won't travel on it. It's just a matter of placing floorguards and doors in the right order.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENThumps move in opposite direction]Also known as moving walls. An example of a map found here. Full explanation highlighted in this thread[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENTeleporters]Detailed instructions on making one here. Also, Infinity has been considered a number. Bug reported here[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENThwump does not move when wedged between two "5" tiles]A thwump does not move when it is enclosed on either side with a "5" tile. Topic here[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENMultiple locked doors overlapped]When multiple locked doors are overlapped, you only need to collect the switch that activates the door that was placed on last[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENDoor+Locked Door]When a normal door is placed under a locked door, with the switch on top, it would be a one-time use platform. Example[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDDrones slow down]Unexplained. Maybe a physics bug. Topic.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUELarge N]It's just freaky. Topic.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEThe alignment is off]Yes, in Ned in Nv1.4, the alignment is a bit off when you place a one-way towards the right or bottom. Hopefully this will be fixed in v1.5. Topic[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDUnexplainable NaN]It's truly a wonder. Invisible platforms, killer tiles, magic locks and trap doors. Topic.[/color]

Glitches/Bugs in Gameplay
Spoiler: [color=GREENTime to complete a level is random/limited]At the beginning of every episode, you start off with 90 seconds. The time you get at the end of every level carries on until the end of the episode[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENGame progress is not saving]Check here. When the game loads, right click the screen, and choose Settings. Choose the tab with the folder on it. Slide the bar all the way to the right (to unlimited)[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENOn userlevels, the game "freezes" when I land on a launchpad and mine at the same time]The 1 frame you land on a launchpad, you are invincible[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENReverse chimney-jumping]If you are close to a wall, and you are facing the opposite direction of the wall, you can still jump. Thread here[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENGold delay]Gold delay is when you place gold over an object to delay the use of it. This does not apply to enemies[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENI get the flavor without completing the last level of a column]Yes, it's true. You can get the flavor without completing the last level in a column. As long as you reach the last level[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEBeing able to play N while in start menu]It's a very strange bug. Topic found here.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEVelocity problems landing on thwump]Usually, when you fall on a vertical moving thwump, you bounce up and down a bit. In this case, it's as if you are glued to the thwump. I have found out that on the moment in which you are standing on the thwump, go in the direction of the wall, and you should be able to hold onto the thwump. Topic found here.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDGame progress erased while in userlevels]This bug hasn't been verified yet. When you attempt to play a userlevels map, it resets the game progress. Exuberance - If you close N while it is writing to a file, it will be corrupted, but it should be able to update the .sol in 1/100th of a second... unless it takes longer because it has to open such a large file maybe.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEHighscoring without actually highscoring]"New online highscore" message displayed frequently while playing. ska - I think that is when you don't have internet access or harveycartel is down.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENBeing able to squeeze through "5" tiles] If you go fast enough, of if forced through, it is possible to go through a 5 tile without dying. Topic here[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEExteme highscores]Yes, sadly, there are major jerks in this world that cheats[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDFloorgaurd doesn't chase you when N is half-snap]When N is literally pixels away from a floorgaurd, it doesn't chase him until he moves farther from the floorgaurd. Topic here[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDLaser goes through tile]This is a strange bug that is yet to be explained. It has been done in this map numerous times. The laser, instead of directing the beam at N, it shoots at a tile. Topic. jtbandes - This happens because the laser hits the tiny, almost unhittable gap between tiles.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEStanding on a wall of thwumps]There hasn't been a solution or explanation to the problem. Similar to the one-way platform bug. Maniac - It's mostly because, by moving left, the ninja is veeeeery slightly adjusting his coordinates to the left, even when he can't actually move left. Since this is a thwump and not, say, a wall, in this case you end up standing on it.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEDrone chases N through door]Yes, if N is next to a door, opening it, and a seeker drone sees him, it will chase N in that direction and through the door[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDInvisible wall-sliding]I don't know how to explain this. It's just remarkable. Topic here[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENN shakes really fast on victory dance]N shakes really fast during a victory dance when he does it on a slope. Topic here[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDRocket sees through walls]My logical explanation is that there is a very small line in between the tiles and that allows the rocket to see through. Topic.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEDouble launchpad boost]It occurs when you press jump at exactly the right point upon contact with a launchpad. Topic.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEGauss malfunction]A gauss aims at N while shooting at a different target. Topic.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=BLUEN dies crashing into the ceiling without enough momentum]Sometimes, N can die crashing into the ceiling without enough momentum. It's very strange, and has yet to be explained.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENUber lag]Lag can do very wierd things. Take this for example. The laser beam is not attached to the laser. Also, lag can creep up as high as it likes. 2434 ms/f anybody?[/color]
Spoiler: [color=REDTimer going into the negatives]The_V_dude - If you play a level in practice mode, it'll record the demo. Sometimes it takes longer than 90 seconds, but that's all recorded. Now if you go watch the demo with practice mode OFF, it'll go into negative time. Topic.[/color]
Spoiler: [color=GREENInvincibility]This occurs in several occasions. The one frame N hits a launchpad, it's invincible. So therefore, if it lands on a mine or an enemy hits it at that particular moment, he seems to be invincible. Only works in userlevels mode.[/color]

I'm been playing this for several months now, and I find it quite fun. It's really simple, and sorta addicting. At the beginning, it's rather boring, but it gets really fun as you progress. Currently I can defeat a Level 9 robot 24/25 times and I can defeat a Level 10 robot 9/10 times and a Level 11 robot 1/2 times.

I'm ranked #85 and creeping up... slowly.
Once you get into the double digits, it's extremely hard to win, because most of these people are insanely good. Sadly, there are quite a few cheaters in this game, but that doesn't mean they have more experience points. You can upgrade, train, and battle your robot. It's pretty fun, I guess. You can spend $5 for more training... sessions. If you want to battle another opponent, you can "hack" onto their account. It's basically seeing what weapons and shields they have, so you can estimate their level of difficulty.

#348602 33 2007-07-29T13:35:35Z usaswim
Quote: 321southpaw, July 29, 2007 04:06 am
@xdude:

The first background was pretty simple.

1. I took the last brush in AxeRaider's Radon brush set and set the color to black.
2. I made a second layer and found a blue color that I liked and made it offset slightly.
3. I took the seventh brush from the Litihium brush set, made it white and layered it over the Radon brush.
4. Used the magic wand and selected the Lithium brush. Then I chose both Radon brush layers and erased the selection.
5. Deselect. Then used the blur tool over the erased section.
6. Did some crazy editing by erasing parts of the Lithium brush to make it look like it was part of the Radon brushes.
7. used some other brush in a set by AxeRaider for the part in the top left. Made a selection that was 3 pixels away from the border and used Stroke to make the inner border.

Oh, the best part: make original dimensions 640x580, then blow it up to 1024x768.

The Basics
Every week, I will give everybody an image to edit. They may do anything they want to it, the only goal is to make it look good or humorous, whichever they think will capture the voters. The voters will be the forumers. At the end of each week (Friday), there will be a poll with all of the entries that week, and it will run throughout the weekend. After 10 weeks, the person with the most points will be declared Metanet Photo Manipulation Champion.

The Rules
  • You can do anything you want with it, like add renders, brushes, and so on.
  • You can only submit 1 entry per round.
  • Entries can not be pornographic in any manner. There are some exceptions.
  • The entry you submit must include this round's image in it.
  • Entries can be of any size.
  • You can PM me your entries, or post them here, whichever way you feel safer.
  • Since a poll can only have up to 10 choices, only the first 10 people to submit their entries will qualify for that round.
  • If less than 3 people enter in a round, I will extend the round 2 more days. If still less than 3 members enter, then the round will be skipped and a new image will be brought in.
  • If your entry receives no votes, you will not get any points for that round.
Judging
The judging system works like this, 1st being most votes -
1st - 5 points
2nd - 4 points
3rd - 3 points
4th - 2 points
5th - 1 point
Everybody else - try harder

In case of a tie for first, a 24 hour poll will be put up. The entry with the most votes will win.
The prize will be an exclusive signature. The second and third place finishers will also recieve an exclusive sig-tag. Everybody else will recieve a sig-tag.

Round 1[/b] - High-res[/b]
Round 2[/b] - Alt link[/b]
Round 3[/b] - High-res[/b]
Round 4[/b] - High-res
Round 5[/b]

#16502 1 2007-08-01T03:03:25Z usaswim
And what really sucks about it is that every single appliance in my house is Kenmore. Except the microwave.

Okay, so here's the story. Just under 6 months ago, we went to Sears and got a refrigerator and a washing machine/dryer to move into our new house. That's when we made the biggest mistake of our lives. Now, present day. Some time ago, when I opened the refrigerator (a side-by-side), there were icicles hanging down from the top. It was like 15F in there! And what next? The (manual) temperature controls are frozen in place. We called Sears repair center, and they sent a guy over. He replaced the water dispenser, God knows why. Nothing was fixed.
In the meantime, our washing machine malfunctioned. We have a Kenmore Oasis, btw. It got to the point where Start became the shutdown button and Power cycled through the wash settings. The main control board screwed up, and a repairman had to replace the entire control panel and the main computer. But guess what? They shipped the wrong part. So we have to wait a few more days for the part to arrive. Also, on the dryer, the computer pretty much screwed up everywhere. I hate the "estimated time remaining" and all of the extra sensors. When we do bedding, it constantly stays at 27 minutes for no particular reason. Anyway, they didn't bother to fix it because they didn't find anything wrong with it.
Back to the refrigerator. A second guy came, and he said that we have to clear out the refrigerator and turn it off overnight, so all the ice can melt. The wall that seperates the freezer from the refrigerator was a big chunk of ice, and prevented any cold air from the freezer to go into the refrigerator. So, the refrigerator stayed at a toasty 65F for a while. Oh, this has happened 2 times since then. Repairing costs $100 everytime.

Lessons learned -
  • Never buy Kenmore. A very unreliable brand.
  • If you buy Kenmore, buy at least 5 years of warranty

#358132 4 2007-08-22T02:48:02Z usaswim
People will play your maps if they look good, that's the most important thing. Also, make them fun. A bunch of random bounce blocks and gold is not considered fun. I suggest you work on your tileset, which is usually the most important part as it is the foundation of the map. A fun tileset will make a better map in the end. You'll have to spend some time on the tileset, they don't take a few minutes. Never make your maps repetitive all the way, as people will get bored really easily. Don't make your maps insanely long. Just by looking at The Great Labyrinth, I wouldn't play it, because judging by the tiles and amount of clutter, it's going to be a really long and tediously boring map. You'll gain more experience over time, and find your own style. Take other people's criticism and try to fix what they don't like.

#359362 6 2007-08-25T22:14:22Z usaswim
Moving Walls

One very special usage of thwumps which many great DDA makers love to use is called the Moving Wall method. Its becoming more common, and was popularized by Lucidiums Pressed for Time. When placed in a specific area, half-way engulfed in a tile, a thwump is placed facing the inside of the wall. See this diagram.



In the diagram above, as long as there is any tile in the red area, the thwump will move in the direction of the arrow when touched. In the last two cases, a little more care is needed when placing the thwumps. They will not obey the special Moving Wall rules if they are placed using 1/2 snap. The third thwump in the diagram must be placed exactly one pixel above its 1/2 snap position to work. The last thwump must be placed exactly one pixel left of its 1/2 snap position to work. Both of these can be done by code-editing. Knowing that the 2 numbers directly after the 8^ represent the x- and y-coordinates of the object, you know how to manipulate its position to move it one pixel in the direction you want (youll be subtracting 1 to do this either way, from the x-coordinate for a leftward moving wall, or from the y-coordinate for an upward moving wall). This is a map with plenty of moving walls to demonstrate their impact in a DDA.


Example

http://metanet.2.forumer.com/index.php?sho...ndpost&p=296005

There's obviously some problems with the code.

    on *:TEXT:away:#: {

      }
    }
    alias -l awaymsg {
      set %text $1-
      if (%text = usaswim) {
        notice $nick Do you want to leave a message?
        notice $nick Choices are "yes" or "no"
      }
    }
    on *:TEXT:yes:*: {
      notice $nick Thank you. Please say your message after the asterick.
      msg $chan *
      timer2 0 1 msreply
    }
    alias -l msreply {

    }
    else {

    }
    on *:TEXT:back:#: {

        msg $chan usaswim is back.

#371942 8 2007-10-14T16:19:18Z usaswim
1. Factorial of a number.
Public Function Factoral(ByVal intnumber As Integer) As Integer
        Dim tempvar As Integer
        tempvar = 1
        For i As Integer = intnumber To 1 Step -1
            tempvar *= i
        Next
        Return tempvar
    End Function

2.1. First 20 Triangular #s
    Private Function tnum(ByVal tri As Integer) As Integer
        Dim trinum As Integer
        For e As Integer = 1 To 20
            trinum += e
        Next
        Return trinum
    End Function

2.2. Determining Triangular #s
    Private Function dettnum(ByVal dettri As Integer) As Boolean
        Dim dettrinum As Integer = 0
        Dim i As Integer
        Dim iDiff As Integer = 1

        While (iDiff > 0)
            dettrinum += i
            iDiff = dettri - dettrinum
            i += 1
        End While

        If iDiff = 0 Then
            Return True
        Else
            Return False
        End If
    End Function

Every graphic designer has done something in their lives that really sparked their imagination and caused them to be interested in what they do.

I remember the first time I ever touched anything related to graphics. I was creating a timeline for a subject, and I wanted to make a circle. Naturally, I could've used Paint, but I found it very inconvenient. I had this software that came with my Dell called Corel Paint Shop Pro. I opened it up and quickly found the shortcut to make a circle. After that, I fooled around with it and I was awed at the things I could make.

It wasn't until I talked to xdude when I found out about Photoshop. I tried it out, and of course, I was confused and unknowing at that time. So, ever since then, I've been using Photoshop. (It was also the time when I learned about torrents and keygens )

So now, it's almost a year since that time, and I'm amazed at how far I've come. I am especially grateful at all the awesome graphic designers here that helped me be where I am today. If I had never been to the Metanet Forums, I would've probably never have pursued graphic designing much further and I would just a normal kid at my school. Since I have started graphic designing, all my teachers have been very impressed at my work on projects, and my friends are all jealous. I'm even getting into web design and CSS, and I've found sorta a "job" in which I can make money out of it.

I'm also erecting a plan to revamp my school's website, which is utter crap in my opinion. A year ago, I wouldn't care, because I had absolutely no taste back then. Now, I look at everything critically.

So, this is one last thanks to the Metanet community, and a special thanks to Harley, who is awesome at everything
